text: The Trans-New Guinea language group includes about 400 languages. By virtue of the number of speakers and the number of languages, it is the largest group of non Austronesian Papuan languages.

title: Abom
text: Abom is a nearly extinct language spoken in the Western Province of Papua New Guinea. According to a 2002 census, only 15 people still speak this language. It has a lexical similarity of 14% with Bitur, 12% with Baramu, 11% with Makayam, 9% with Were, and 4% with Idi and Agob.
